maria.gonzalez: Heads-up — onboarding ceres-7b-qlora into the eval harness. CI job intermittently fails the runner stage with token-splitting mismatches on our chat templates :eyes:. Not sure if it's the tokenizer or the chat template preprocessor.

kenji.tanaka: Ugh, saw that yesterday. Fail looks like: expected 1 extra token in middle of system prompt after quantize pass. Can you paste the failing log snippet? :face_with_monocle:

maria.gonzalez: Pasting the minimal failing log from the CI run:
```
ERROR runner.tests.test_token_consistency - mismatch at pos 23
expected_tokens: ['▁Hello', ',', '▁my', '▁name', '▁is', '▁ceres']
actual_tokens:   ['Hello', ',', '▁my', '▁name', '▁is', '▁ceres']
```
Looks like a leading underscore missing for token 0 in actual_tokens. The harness uses our TokenizerWrapper (hf tokenizer w/bytelevel fallback).

oliver.smith: Could be the tokenizer being swapped by quantized model code path or an older tokenizer.json in the model repo. Did the onboarding job pull artifacts from model-storage v2 or v3?

maria.gonzalez: Onboarding script used model manifest ref `models/ceres/ceres-7b-qlora@rev-2026-03-12`. That repo had tokenizer.json updated by the quant team.

ci-bot: CI job #4821: runner-stage failed 3/10 attempts. Flaky failure pattern detected (failure rate 30%). Attached run IDs: r4821-1, r4821-3.

kenji.tanaka: I reproduced locally with the exact manifest. Quick diff between HF tokenizer.encode outputs and our wrapper:
```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
t = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json')
print(t.encode('Hello, my name is ceres').tokens)
# -> ['Hello', ',', '▁my', '▁name', '▁is', '▁ceres']
```
HF tokenizer returns 'Hello' without leading underline when using byte-level. Our harness expects '▁Hello'. So the mismatch is real.

sophia.raj: That explains the test — the eval runner canonicalizes tokens with `normalize_tokens()` which currently assumes leading space tokens. Need to make it robust to both byte-level and sentencepiece-style outputs.

zach.long: Two actionable ideas: 1) Normalize at harness boundary: call tokenizer.pre_tokenize or apply `add_leading_underscore_if_missing()` for first token when template starts with no whitespace. 2) Gate the onboarding: require tokenizer version pin in model manifest and add unit that compares hf tokenizer vs saved tokenizer.json. Prefer 2 for safety.

maria.gonzalez: Agreed. Short-term patch: relax the CI test to compare normalized text using join(token list) instead of token-by-token exact match (so we avoid spurious fails). Long-term: add a tokenizer-consistency job that runs during model manifest PR with explicit accepted tokenization modes.

oliver.smith: I'll open a small PR to the eval harness:
- Add helper `tokenization_mode` ("sentencepiece" | "byte-level" | "legacy") per model manifest.
- Update runner test to consult mode and normalize accordingly.
- Add a gating unit test in CI to compare `hf_tokenizer.encode(text).tokens` vs `saved_tokenizer.encode(text).tokens` and flag if tokenization_mode missing.

kenji.tanaka: Can we also log the tokenizer config (pre-tokenizer, normalizer) in onboarding logs so ops can diagnose faster? Put a small JSON dump in the onboarding artifacts.

maria.gonzalez: Yes — will add tokenizer.json snapshot to artifacts for the next onboarding run. For the short-term CI patch, I'm going to: 1) relax comparison, 2) add a flaky-run counter to ignore transient quant path race. Will push PR in ~30m.

sophia.raj: Note: chat templates can introduce leading/trailing whitespace depending on placeholder expansion ({{user_input}} may be empty). We should canonicalize templates by running them through `render_template(...).lstrip()` before tokenization.

zach.long: Good call. Also add a small template unit test in harness that ensures system & user messages are rendered consistently for empty/edge placeholders.

maria.gonzalez: PR 997 opened: tiny changes to runner test and added logging. Marking onboarding job to re-run. Will follow up with manifest pin request to model owners for tokenizer_mode + tokenizer_hash. :shipit:

ci-bot: CI job #4821 rerun -> r4821-4: runner-stage passed. Final status: onboarding job passed on attempt 4.

kenji.tanaka: Nice. Follow-ups: create a short doc in docs/eval-harness about tokenizer modes and update the onboarding checklist. I'll draft.

maria.gonzalez: Thanks team — leaving a note for postmortem: flaky caused by tokenizer-mode drift after quant team's tokenizer.json migration. Will loop in quant team to sync manifests.

sophia.raj: cc @quant-team for visibility.
